# Vector Field Projection onto Surface

Also called: Normal projection, Projections for Particle Traces, Vieweye projection, XY normal projection

## Overview
This family defines methods for projecting a 3D vector onto a 2D surface to determine the direction of particle trace segments, as required by [Particle Traces on 2D Surfaces](12772-particle-traces-on-2d-surfaces.md) [S1, unofficial]. The primary distinction among siblings is viewpoint dependency: normal, xy normal, and cylinder projections are viewpoint independent, while the vieweye projection requires recalculation when the viewpoint changes [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All techniques in this family operate on a 3D vector $\mathbf{v}$ at a point $\mathbf{p}$ on a 2D surface [G]. The goal is to compute a 2D direction vector $\mathbf{d}$ tangent to the surface at $\mathbf{p}$, which represents the projected flow direction [G]. The surface is assumed to be defined such that its normal $\mathbf{n}$ at $\mathbf{p}$ is available [G]. The resulting direction $\mathbf{d}$ is used to orient the particle trace segments [G].

## Subtopics

### Normal Projection
Normal projection projects the 3D vector at a point on the surface onto the surface in a direction parallel to the surface normal at that point [S1, unofficial]. This technique is viewpoint independent [S1, unofficial]. It is straightforward but can yield unintuitive particle traces [S1, unofficial].

### XY Normal Projection
The XY normal projection is designed for producing film loops where the viewpoint is rotated about the z (vertical) axis [S1, unofficial]. It projects the vector onto the surface using the XY plane normal [G]. Like the normal projection, it is viewpoint independent [S1, unofficial].

### Cylinder Projection
[Cylinder projection](#12798-cylinder-projection.md) is a viewpoint-independent technique [S1, unofficial]. It projects the 3D vector onto the surface along a direction defined by a cylinder axis, typically aligned with the vertical axis [G].

### Vieweye Projection
The vieweye projection is viewpoint dependent [S1, unofficial]. It projects the 3D vector onto the surface relative to the current camera viewpoint [G]. Consequently, the particle traces must be recalculated every time the viewpoint changes [S1, unofficial].

## Background
This family of techniques originates from research into visualizing 3D velocity fields near contour surfaces [S1, unofficial]. The specific comparison of these four [projection methods](#6890-ray-traversal-schemes.md) (normal, xy normal, cylinder, and vieweye) was conducted to evaluate their ability to indicate 3D flow on 2D surfaces [S1, unofficial]. The study used a simple test case of a constant velocity field to assess the intuitiveness of the resulting particle traces [S1, unofficial].

## Sources
